_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x15-rc-input.json and opened no other file, repository search, web page or API.

hints.reason: ALIEN via the History channel's Ancient Aliens (a huge meme), HISTORY via 'ancient history' and the channel itself; clicks right away.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pop-culture double route on the HISTORY side.

hints.reason: ARM via the armless Venus de Milo, PLANET via Venus itself; a classic aha, and both facts (armless, hottest planet) are true.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent indirect-knowledge hint.

hints.reason: BAG via the golf caddy carrying the bag, TEA via a tea caddy tin; a real double meaning, though 'tea caddy' is less familiar to U.S. players than to British ones.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: tea caddy is known in the U.S. but leans British; golf usually spells it 'caddie' (caddy is an accepted variant).

hints.reason: BAND via Oasis of 'Wonderwall', DESERT via a desert oasis; a clean, famous double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Ideal double meaning.

hints.reason: BARK and BITE are both things a dog does, sealed by the saying 'bark is worse than his bite'; easy but clean.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; may also pull other dog-related board words, but the idiom anchors both.

hints.reason: BATTERY via jumper cables for a dead battery, SHOT via the basketball jumper (jump shot); a satisfying two-sense click.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning.

hints.reason: BILL via the restaurant check, CHESS via check/checkmate; clean, familiar double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Solid classic.

hints.reason: MOON via a lunar eclipse, BLOOD via the red 'blood moon' a total lunar eclipse produces; the BLOOD side is one step further but widely known now.

pairs.pair_note: BLOOD side relies on the 'blood moon' term; SUN on the board could compete for the second word.

hints.reason: BOLT via Harry Potter's lightning-bolt scar, LION via Scar of The Lion King; a satisfying indirect aha.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: BUBBLE via popping a bubble, FATHER via Pop as a name for Dad; clean and easy.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning.

hints.reason: RED via Mars the Red Planet, CANDY via Mars Inc. (M&M's, Snickers); true and fair.

pairs.pair_note: MARS is also the hint for p_chocolate__war; avoid serving both close together.

hints.reason: CAT via Tom of Tom and Jerry and 'tomcat', THUMB via the Tom Thumb tale; both instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: CHALLENGE via the figurative hurdle, TRACK via hurdles as a track event; the synonym side is backed by a real second sense.

pairs.pair_note: Clean literal/figurative double.

hints.reason: WAR via Mars the Roman god of war, CHOCOLATE via the Mars bar and Mars candy company; the god-of-war side gives a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: The Mars bar itself is less common in U.S. stores than in the U.K., but the Mars company is well known; same hint word as p_candy__red.

hints.reason: CIRCUS via Barnum's circus, SHOW via 'The Greatest Show on Earth' (and The Greatest Showman); accurate and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Good historical/pop-culture hint.

hints.reason: CLOWN via Batman's clown-faced Joker (and joker as a jester), WILD via 'jokers wild'; a satisfying double.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: POLAR via The Polar Express, CONDUCTOR via the express train's (and the film's famous) conductor; fair and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: POLAR side is a phrase completion; CONDUCTOR side has a real train route too.

hints.reason: CRASH via rebooting a crashed computer, FILM via franchise reboots; a modern, satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: CROSS via X as a cross shape, TREASURE via 'X marks the spot'; a crisp one-letter hint that clicks.

pairs.pair_note: Confirm one-letter hints are allowed by the game UI.

hints.reason: DESSERT via the final course of a meal, GOLF via the golf course; clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: DOCTOR via Doctor Who, FIRST via Abbott and Costello's 'Who's on First?'; both phrases are instantly familiar and the pairing is fun.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join worth keeping.

hints.reason: DRILL via 'drill sergeant', SOLDIER via sergeant as a soldier's rank; honest and clear, if flat.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and unexciting but fair; no clearly better hint comes to mind.

hints.reason: EASTER via Easter egg, ROLL via egg roll, tied together by the White House Easter Egg Roll; instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join made nicer by the Easter Egg Roll bonus.

hints.reason: FAIRY via Tinker Bell the fairy, PAN via Peter Pan's companion (with a bonus pots-and-pans tinker link); true and easy.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: the official name is two words, 'Tinker Bell'; the run-together spelling is common but may trip the one-word rule.

hints.reason: FASHION via Coco Chanel, MEXICO via Pixar's Coco and its Day of the Dead setting; a lovely two-reference aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; 'created the little black dress' is the popular framing (she popularized it), acceptable.

hints.reason: FIREWORKS via the Fourth of July, STAR WARS via 'May the Fourth be with you'; a fun date-based aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: FRUIT via the botanical classification, VEGETABLE via kitchen usage; the famous fruit-or-vegetable debate.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and accurate.

hints.reason: STRONG via Samson's legendary strength, HAIR via losing it when his hair was cut; accurate and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: HOOK and LINE via the idiom 'hook, line and sinker' and the fishing rig itself; the phrase is instantly familiar and completing it is satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; ROD or other fishing words on the board could compete.

hints.reason: JAM and PICKLE both come in jars, which is true but unremarkable (honey, salsa and peanut butter do too), while 'in a jam' / 'in a pickle' offers a much more satisfying shared idiom that this hint does not use.
hints.fix: Jam and pickles are both sold in glass jars.

pairs.pair_note: The pair's real aha is the trouble idiom (TROUBLE or FIX); the current explanation mentions it, but that route does not run through JAR, which muddles the reveal.

hints.reason: KIWI via its fuzzy skin, POLICE via 'the fuzz' slang; older slang but widely known, and a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: MARIO via the Koopa Troopa enemies (and King Koopa), SHELL via kicking Koopa shells; accurate, and Mario is broad enough that 'Koopa' lands for most players.

pairs.pair_note: Moderate recognizability for non-gamers; still fair given how famous Mario is.

hints.reason: Both MINT and THIN via Thin Mints, the best-known Girl Scout cookie; an indirect route with a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect route; COOKIE would be flatter.

hints.reason: NINJA via Shredder, the Ninja Turtles' Foot Clan leader, PAPER via a paper shredder; a fun double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: PASS via the famous 'You shall not pass!', STAFF via Gandalf's wizard staff struck on the bridge; one iconic scene covers both.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the quote is the film wording (the book has 'You cannot pass'), which is fine.

hints.reason: SPY via a planted listening bug, PLANT via insects eating plants and the bonus verb 'plant a bug'; a neat layered double.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; 'spies plant bugs' gives PLANT a second, cleverer route.

hints.reason: RABBIT via Elmer Fudd hunting Bugs Bunny, SEASON via the 'Rabbit season! Duck season!' gag (and hunting season); a nostalgic aha.

pairs.pair_note: SEASON side depends on knowing the gag, but it is widely known and hunting season backs it up.

hints.reason: A Roomba is literally a robot vacuum, so ROBOT and VACUUM both come straight to mind; easy but satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Easy brand hint; fine.

hints.reason: TORNADO via the Kansas twister that carries Dorothy to Oz, SCARECROW via her companion; accurate and instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Good; OZ would be an equally fair alternative.

hints.reason: SNAKE via Medusa's snake hair, STONE via her petrifying gaze; accurate and familiar myth.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: SPONGEBOB via the villain Plankton, WHALE via whales feeding on plankton; a fun character/science double.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the show even has a whale (Pearl), a small bonus.

hints.reason: WING via Icarus's wax-and-feather wings, SUN via flying too close to it; accurate, well-known myth.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: WORK via the boss at your job, VIDEO GAME via the end-of-level boss fight; clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good.
